subject: Dedicated pool SLA: tail-latency and burst-reservation clarification
messages:
From: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@helixaipro.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@acme-procurement.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated pool - tail latency & burst reservations

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — HelixAI is excited about the performance profile on the dedicated nodes. Before we move to contract, our infra and procurement teams asked for two clarifications to include in the SLA addendum:

1) Tail latency carve-out: we run a mix of short chat queries and long-context classification. Can Redwood confirm whether a tail-latency SLA (p99 over 1-minute window) can be guaranteed for the reserved pool, or if we should expect queueing behavior to be used to preserve throughput SLOs? If queued requests are expected, can you outline any maximum queue wait time or backpressure behavior?

2) Burst reservations handshake: HelixAI needs predictable burst capacity if our traffic spikes (up to 3x baseline for bursts up to 2 minutes). We want to understand how burst reservations are honored for reserved GPUs versus shared capacity and whether a short preemption window or provisioning handshake could add latency to the first tokens.

I attached a short sample of our request distribution and a draft addendum (attached) for your legal team to review. Can you loop in someone in product or SRE who can confirm expected behavior so we can finalize procurement?

Thanks,
Maya Thompson
Head of Infrastructure, HelixAI
maya.thompson@helixaipro.com

Attachments: HelixAI_SLA_Addendum_v1.pdf, helix_queue_profile_nov2026.csv

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@helixaipro.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool - tail latency & burst reservations

Hi Maya — appreciate the clear ask and the attach. Looping in Laura (Sales Eng) and Marissa (Product ops) to confirm the operational behavior. Quick answers up front:

- Reserved pools are prioritized for your tenant; we do not route bursts to shared hosted capacity unless configured as a failover.
- We don’t publish a hard p99 tail-latency SLA today for variable long-context workloads because tail events can come from model sequence-length spikes and KV-cache misses. That said, we can define a contractual carve-out and a maximum queue wait objective for requests that exceed concurrent allocation.

Laura/Marissa — can you confirm (1) typical queue wait limits we can offer as an objective for an addendum and (2) the behavior of the burst reservation handshake (provisioning time + first-token latency expectations) so I can feed that back to Helix?

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@helixaipro.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T13:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool - tail latency & burst reservations

Maya — quick operational summary from Product/SRE:

- Dedicated pool prioritization: Reserved GPUs are pinned to your tenant and pre-warmed. For steady-state concurrency up to the reserved allocation, we can guarantee p50/p95 latency numbers that match the catalog profile.
- Tail-latency carve-out approach: We recommend offering a contractual target for p99 over a 5-minute rolling window with an explicit carve-out for model-initiated long sequences and cold-cache scenarios. Practically, our proposed SLA language would: 
  * Guarantee p99 <= X ms for sequences up to Y tokens under typical cache hit rates;
  * Define carve-outs for model sequence length spikes and full-cache misses (we can insert example thresholds).
- Queueing/backpressure: If concurrent requests exceed your reserved concurrency, we will queue up to a configurable maximum wait time. Suggested objective for the addendum: max wait = 12s (99th percentile) for short chat calls, after which requests will be rejected with a defined error code so clients can fallback. This keeps node saturation predictable and avoids noisy neighbor slowdowns.
- Burst reservation handshake: Provisioning of burst capacity from idle reserved spare nodes is near-instant (<2s) for warm pools; if new nodes must be provisioned from cloud, we expect a 20–45s window for readiness — first-token latency may increase during that provisioning window. For your use-case (2-minute spikes), we can propose a hybrid policy: guarantee instant burst from reserved warm spare capacity up to 2x baseline, with a secondary provisioning tier for larger bursts (20–45s).

I’ve attached a proposed addendum clause (see markup) with exact numeric suggestions. If those numbers look reasonable, Marissa can shepherd an SLA addendum for legal.

—Laura
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@acme-procurement.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@helixaipro.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool - tail latency & burst reservations

Thanks — the procurement team prefers concrete, deterministic SLAs for financial modeling. A few follow-ups:

1) If you publish the p99 numeric and a carve-out definition, can you include a credit formula for sustained breaches (e.g., >3 outages per quarter or p99 > threshold for >30m cumulative)?
2) For the 12s max wait objective, can you confirm whether time spent waiting is counted against client request timeouts and whether we can configure server-side retry hints?

We can accept a hybrid burst policy if there is a clear numeric guarantee for the warm spare pool and a maximum provisioning time for cold adds. Please include those in the draft addendum so our legal can review.

Regards,
Jorge Alvarez
Head of Procurement, Acme (on behalf of HelixAI)

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@helixaipro.com>, Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@acme-procurement.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-07T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool - tail latency & burst reservations

Maya/Jorge — thanks for the feedback. We took the ask to SRE/legal and drafted concrete language for the addendum. Highlights: 

- p99 target: 450ms for sequences <= 2048 tokens, measured over 5-minute rolling windows, subject to carve-outs for model sequence length > 2048 tokens or full KV-cache miss events.
- Queue wait objective: 99th percentile wait <= 12s. After 12s the request will be rejected with error code 429 + "POOL_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED" and we will log the event for credit evaluation.
- Burst policy: Warm-spare guarantee: up to 2x baseline instantaneous capacity with first-token latency within catalog p95. Cold-provisioning maximum readiness time 45s (measured from request for burst to node-ready), during which first-token latency may be elevated; we will prioritize warm spares before cold provisioning.
- Credit formula (proposed): If p99 threshold breached for >30 continuous minutes or cumulative >90 minutes in a rolling 90-day window, customer is eligible for service credits pro-rated to affected reserved units (calculation in draft addendum).

Attached: updated addendum PDF (HelixAI_SLA_Addendum_v1 - redlined) and the queue profile you sent. If this matches, Rishi — please propose a next step (legal review/DocuSign) and we’ll shepherd signature.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: HelixAI_SLA_Addendum_v1.pdf, helix_queue_profile_nov2026.csv
